title: NCBI rRNA Submission Protocol
author: Avery S Hiley
materials: In this example, “A9919” is the BIC number; use either the BIC number or a different institution’s catalog number here to represent the sequence ID. If catalog numbers are not assigned yet, you may use a lab code (e.g. S25170) as the sequence ID here.
“Peinaleopolynoe mineoi”: Repeat the species name here.

“voucher SIO:BIC:A9919”: Follow this proper format to identify the corresponding BIC number with our institution abbreviations. If the specimen is deposited at a different institution, this will instead mimic the abbreviations of that place before listing the catalog number (e.g. MNHN for Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle). If your catalog numbers aren’t assigned yet, exclude this section altogether.

Source Info : Under ‘Do your sequence IDs represent one of these?’, select ‘Specimen-Voucher’ if you followed the headers format in step 15. If catalog numbers aren’t assigned yet and your sequence IDs were listed as lab codes (e.g. S25147), select ‘Isolate’ here.

“voucher SIO:BIC:A9919”: Follow this proper format to identify the corresponding BIC number with our institution abbreviations. If the specimen is deposited at a different institution, this will instead mimic the abbreviations of that place before listing the catalog number (e.g. MNHN for Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle). If your catalog numbers aren’t assigned yet, exclude this section altogether.

steps.title: Align rRNA Sequences
steps.instruction: Gather rRNA sequences (e.g., mitochondrial 16S, 12S and nuclear 18S, 28S) and align them using Geneious, Mesquite, or the online MAFFT version 7 server (https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/server/).

substeps.instruction: Align and submit each rRNA gene separately.

steps.title: Verify Sequence Orientation
steps.instruction: Blast one of the sequences on NCBI to ensure the first matching record says 'Plus/Plus', indicating the correct forward 5' direction.

substeps.instruction: If the record says 'Plus/Minus', reverse complement the entire alignment.

steps.title: Resolve Sequence Ambiguities
steps.instruction: Ensure there are no ambiguities (non-ACGT bases like N, K, M, or other IUPAC codes) in the sequences.

substeps.instruction: Review the original De Novo assembly in Geneious to attempt a nucleotide base call.
Compare Forward/Reverse peak amplitudes in the chromatogram (.ab1 files) and select the nucleotide with the greater amplitude.
Trim the ends of the sequence assembly if quality is low or poor.
Perform any necessary nucleotide edits or deletions.

steps.title: Export Alignment
steps.instruction: Export the final alignment from Mesquite as a fasta file.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the 'include gaps' option is NOT selected.

steps.title: Format Sequence Headers
steps.instruction: Open the fasta file in TextWrangler or BBEdit and edit all sequence headers to the following format: >A9919 [organism=Peinaleopolynoe mineoi] Peinaleopolynoe mineoi voucher SIO:BIC:A9919 cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene, partial cds; mitochondrial

substeps.instruction: Insert the specific species name for the corresponding sequence ID in the [organism=...] section.
Ensure 'cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene, partial cds; mitochondrial' is listed at the end of the header information.

steps.title: Prepare NCBI Submission Account
steps.instruction: Create an account for the NCBI Submission Portal at https://submit.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.

steps.title: Enter Submitter Information
steps.instruction: Fill out the Submitter information and check 'Update my contact information in profile' to set these details as the default for future submissions.

steps.title: Specify Sequencing Technology
steps.instruction: Under Sequencing Technology, select 'Sanger dideoxy sequencing' and 'Assembled sequences (each sequence was assembled from two or more overlapping sequence reads)'.

steps.title: Upload Sequences
steps.instruction: Upload the completed COI fasta file.

substeps.instruction: Under Sequences, select 'Release on specified date or upon publication, whichever is first' (typically choosing a year in advance) or select 'release immediately' if the upload is late.

steps.title: Apply Source Modifiers
steps.instruction: Add key details to the sequences. While organism name and specimen-voucher are required (and should already be in the headers), you may add locality (Country) and depth (Altitude).

substeps.instruction: Option 1: Upload a tab-delimited table. Download the template and edit in TextEdit, TextWrangler, BBEdit, or Excel. Separate columns with 1 tab. Format 'Country' from broad to specific (e.g., 'Costa Rica: Mound 12') and enter 'Altitude' as negative values (e.g., '-1800 m').
Option 2: Use the editable table via the online interface to manually add columns. Copy and save this work externally for records.

steps.title: Add References and Authors
steps.instruction: Under 'Sequence authors', add yourself (or the person who performed the lab work).

substeps.instruction: Add the title of the paper.
Use 'Specify new authors' to add all authors on the paper.

steps.title: Review and Submit
steps.instruction: Review all submission details and submit the sequences.
